_doc: Teacher goal bank for the Teacher Hub. Student-facing wording in the lab's own words (not WIDA text), grouped by the three WIDA language dimensions. Each goal names the evidence the lab already collects for it: a skill node (skill-graph.js), a conference need (teacher.js CONFERENCE_NEEDS) or an error pattern (detective/patterns.json). Counts only; a goal never becomes a level or a score. `tryTomorrow` is a three-to-five-minute teaching move, in teacher-facing English, shown for any goal not yet shown on the student's own.

goals.en: I can say the main idea of what I heard.
goals.es: Puedo decir la idea principal de lo que escuché.
goals.tryTomorrow: Play a 30-second clip. Pause and ask for the main idea in one sentence. Then play it again and ask which words were a clue.

goals.en: I can name details that support the main idea.
goals.es: Puedo nombrar detalles que apoyan la idea principal.
goals.tryTomorrow: After a short listen, ask for the main idea first, then two details that prove it. Have the student hold up fingers as each detail is named.

goals.en: I can follow directions that have more than one step.
goals.es: Puedo seguir instrucciones que tienen más de un paso.
goals.tryTomorrow: Give a three-step direction aloud once. The student draws or acts out each step in order, then says the steps back using first, next, last.

goals.en: I can put what I heard in the right order.
goals.es: Puedo poner en orden lo que escuché.
goals.tryTomorrow: Read four sentences from a short story out of order. The student numbers them as they hear time words such as first, then, finally.

goals.en: I can tell why something happened, from what I heard.
goals.es: Puedo decir por qué pasó algo, según lo que escuché.
goals.tryTomorrow: Play a short explanation. Ask: What happened? Why did it happen? Have the student answer in one sentence with because.

goals.en: I can work out a new word from how it is used.
goals.es: Puedo deducir una palabra nueva por cómo se usa.
goals.tryTomorrow: Say a sentence with one unfamiliar word. Ask what the other words suggest it means. Check the guess against the word bank.

goals.en: I can find the main idea of a text.
goals.es: Puedo encontrar la idea principal de un texto.
goals.tryTomorrow: Cover everything but the title and first sentence. Ask for the main idea. Then uncover one paragraph at a time and ask if the idea still fits.

goals.en: I can find the sentence that proves my answer.
goals.es: Puedo encontrar la oración que prueba mi respuesta.
goals.tryTomorrow: Ask a question about a short text. The student underlines the one sentence that answers it and reads it aloud before explaining.

goals.en: I can explain how my evidence supports my idea.
goals.es: Puedo explicar cómo mi evidencia apoya mi idea.
goals.tryTomorrow: Give the student a quote. Use the frame: This shows that … because … . Have them say it aloud, then write it.

goals.en: I can use the words around a new word to work out its meaning.
goals.es: Puedo usar las palabras alrededor de una palabra nueva para deducir su significado.
goals.tryTomorrow: Choose one hard word in a passage. Circle the clues in the two sentences around it and decide on a meaning together, then check it.

goals.en: I can use clues in the text to figure out what it does not say.
goals.es: Puedo usar pistas del texto para deducir lo que no dice.
goals.tryTomorrow: Ask a question the text does not answer directly. The student writes the clue from the text, what they already know, and their inference.

goals.en: I can summarize the most important information.
goals.es: Puedo resumir la información más importante.
goals.tryTomorrow: After reading, the student crosses out details until three key points remain, then says the summary using first, then, finally.

goals.en: I can use word parts to work out a new word.
goals.es: Puedo usar las partes de una palabra para deducir una palabra nueva.
goals.tryTomorrow: Write a word with a prefix or suffix. Split it into parts, say what each part means, then rebuild the meaning of the whole word.

goals.en: I can reread a text with a purpose.
goals.es: Puedo releer un texto con un propósito.
goals.tryTomorrow: Before a second read, set one purpose: find the cause, find the evidence, or find the order. Read again only for that purpose.

goals.en: I can compare what two sources say.
goals.es: Puedo comparar lo que dicen dos fuentes.
goals.tryTomorrow: Give two short texts on one topic. The student fills a two-column chart, then says one way they are the same and one way they differ.

goals.en: I can say one clear idea so a listener understands it.
goals.es: Puedo decir una idea clara para que quien me escucha la entienda.
goals.tryTomorrow: Ask one question. The student answers in a single clear sentence, then repeats it more slowly. A partner says it back to check understanding.

goals.en: I can add details that help my listener.
goals.es: Puedo agregar detalles que ayudan a quien me escucha.
goals.tryTomorrow: After a one-sentence answer, ask Tell me more about … twice. The student adds a detail each time, then says the whole answer together.

goals.en: I can say why I think what I think.
goals.es: Puedo decir por qué pienso lo que pienso.
goals.tryTomorrow: Ask for an opinion. The student answers with I think … because … . A partner asks Why? once and the student adds a second reason.

goals.en: I can use evidence when I speak.
goals.es: Puedo usar evidencia cuando hablo.
goals.tryTomorrow: Give a short chart or text. The student says a claim, then points to one number or phrase with According to … .

goals.en: I can connect my ideas in an order that makes sense.
goals.es: Puedo conectar mis ideas en un orden que tenga sentido.
goals.tryTomorrow: Name three events from a short text. The student retells them with first, next, finally, then changes the order and retells again.

goals.en: I can use exact words from the topic.
goals.es: Puedo usar palabras exactas del tema.
goals.tryTomorrow: Pick three topic words from the word bank. The student uses each in a spoken sentence and replaces any vague word with one of them.

goals.en: I can make my spoken sentences longer with more than one idea.
goals.es: Puedo hacer mis oraciones habladas más largas, con más de una idea.
goals.tryTomorrow: Start with a short sentence. Add because, but or so to make it longer. Say the new sentence twice, then add a detail.

goals.en: I can answer exactly what the prompt asks.
goals.es: Puedo responder justo lo que pide la pregunta.
goals.tryTomorrow: Underline the verb in the prompt and circle what it asks for. The student says in their own words what to do before writing.

goals.en: I can state my central idea clearly.
goals.es: Puedo expresar mi idea central con claridad.
goals.tryTomorrow: Before drafting, the student writes the central idea as one sentence and checks that every later sentence supports it.

goals.en: I can organize my information so a reader can follow it.
goals.es: Puedo organizar mi información para que un lector la siga.
goals.tryTomorrow: Use a three-box organizer: beginning, middle, end (or claim, evidence, explanation). Fill it in aloud before writing the paragraph.

goals.en: I can include evidence that fits my claim.
goals.es: Puedo incluir evidencia que encaje con mi afirmación.
goals.tryTomorrow: Read the claim. The student finds one detail in the source that fits and copies it exactly with quotation marks.

goals.en: I can explain my evidence instead of only copying it.
goals.es: Puedo explicar mi evidencia en vez de solo copiarla.
goals.tryTomorrow: After a quote, add a sentence starting with This shows … . Compare two student sentences and choose the one that explains.

goals.en: I can use joining words that fit.
goals.es: Puedo usar palabras de enlace que encajen.
goals.tryTomorrow: Give two sentences. The student chooses a joining word (because, however, for example) and says why it fits before writing.

goals.en: I can use academic words from the topic.
goals.es: Puedo usar palabras académicas del tema.
goals.tryTomorrow: Highlight three topic words from the word bank. Rewrite a plain sentence so it uses at least two of them.

goals.en: I can write longer sentences with more than one idea.
goals.es: Puedo escribir oraciones más largas, con más de una idea.
goals.tryTomorrow: Take one short sentence. Add who, when, where and why in turn, one piece at a time, until it is a full expanded sentence.

goals.en: I can revise my writing so it is clearer.
goals.es: Puedo revisar mi escritura para que sea más clara.
goals.tryTomorrow: The student reads their draft aloud and stops where it does not make sense. Fix one sentence at a time, then read again.

goals.en: I can write on my own, with only the supports I choose.
goals.es: Puedo escribir por mi cuenta, solo con los apoyos que yo elija.
goals.tryTomorrow: Choose On my own for the next task. Afterwards the student lists which supports they wanted and when they would have used them.

goals.en: I link my ideas in at least two different ways when I explain.
goals.es: Conecto mis ideas de al menos dos maneras distintas cuando explico.
goals.tryTomorrow: Show two sentences with no link. Add because, as a result and however in turn and name the job each word does.

goals.en: I keep past events in the past tense when I tell what happened.
goals.es: Mantengo los hechos pasados en tiempo pasado cuando cuento lo que ocurrió.
goals.tryTomorrow: Underline the time words in a retell. Check that each verb after one is in the past tense, and fix any that is not.

goals.en: I name where my evidence comes from when I make a claim.
goals.es: Digo de dónde viene mi evidencia cuando hago una afirmación.
goals.tryTomorrow: Add According to … or The data shows … before each piece of evidence, naming where it came from.

goals.en: I use at least two exact subject words when I inform.
goals.es: Uso al menos dos palabras exactas del tema cuando informo.
goals.tryTomorrow: Replace thing, stuff and a lot with exact words from the source. Read both versions aloud and compare.

goals.en: I put -s on the verb after he, she or it.
goals.es: Pongo -s en el verbo después de he, she o it.
goals.tryTomorrow: Write five sentences about one person. Circle each verb and add -s after he, she or it, then read them aloud.

goals.en: I choose am, is or are to match my subject.
goals.es: Elijo am, is o are para que concuerde con mi sujeto.
goals.tryTomorrow: Say sentences with I, he, they and the dogs, choosing am, is or are each time. Write three of them and read them aloud.

goals.en: I use a past verb after a past-time word like yesterday.
goals.es: Uso un verbo en pasado después de una palabra de tiempo pasado como yesterday.
goals.tryTomorrow: Circle past-time words (yesterday, last week). Check that the verb in the same sentence is in the past form.

goals.en: I use the right form of irregular past verbs.
goals.es: Uso la forma correcta de los verbos irregulares en pasado.
goals.tryTomorrow: Keep a short list of irregular verbs the student actually uses (go–went, see–saw). Use two of them in new sentences today.

goals.en: I make the noun plural after a number.
goals.es: Pongo el sustantivo en plural después de un número.
goals.tryTomorrow: Write ten phrases from the text with a number and a noun (one dog, three dogs). Label each singular or plural and read them aloud.

goals.en: I choose a or an by the sound that comes next.
goals.es: Elijo a o an según el sonido que sigue.
goals.tryTomorrow: Say the word, listen to its first sound, then choose a or an. Write ten words with the right article.

goals.en: I use do, does or did with the plain verb in questions and negatives.
goals.es: Uso do, does o did con el verbo simple en preguntas y negaciones.
goals.tryTomorrow: Turn five statements into questions and negatives using do, does or did, keeping the main verb plain.

goals.en: I put the words of a question in the right order.
goals.es: Pongo las palabras de una pregunta en el orden correcto.
goals.tryTomorrow: Say the parts of a question in order: question word, helper verb, subject, main verb. Write the question, then ask a partner.

goals.en: I finish a sentence that starts with because or when.
goals.es: Termino una oración que empieza con because o when.
goals.tryTomorrow: Show a sentence that starts with because and stops. Add the missing main idea and read the whole sentence aloud.

goals.en: I do not join two sentences with only a comma.
goals.es: No uno dos oraciones solo con una coma.
goals.tryTomorrow: Find two sentences joined by a comma. Fix it three ways: a period, and/but/so, or because/when.

goals.en: I use capital letters and end punctuation.
goals.es: Uso mayúsculas y puntuación final.
goals.tryTomorrow: Read a short paragraph aloud and have the student touch each place a capital or an end mark is needed.

goals.en: I choose the preposition English uses.
goals.es: Elijo la preposición que usa el inglés.
goals.tryTomorrow: Collect three phrases that need in, on or at. Write the correct phrase and a short sentence for each.

goals.en: I replace vague words with exact ones.
goals.es: Reemplazo palabras vagas por palabras exactas.
goals.tryTomorrow: Circle vague words (thing, good, a lot) in a draft. Choose a more exact word for each from the word bank.

goals.en: I use joining words in the right form.
goals.es: Uso las palabras de enlace en la forma correcta.
goals.tryTomorrow: Match joining words to the job they do (reason, contrast, order). Rewrite one sentence three ways.
